description: Skelet AC-00 perf baseline: board-adjacent read benchmark script with CI schema proof (no gates, environment-relative)

compatibility.instructions: Does this grain preserve all contracts: no product code, schema, API, MCP, migration, donor, or config change; one new script plus one new node test auto-wired into the existing web CI glob? Any changed behavior?

correctness.instructions: Is the benchmark correct: fixed synthetic corpus with deterministic titles, actor-scoped reads on the same functions the transports serve, warm-up before sampling, p50/p95/max over fixed iterations, result sizes proving non-empty coverage of all four ops? Does the CI test prove the script exits zero and emits the exact schema with sane ordering (p50 within p95 within max)?

evidence.instructions: Is evidence sufficient: full-size run recorded (list_flows p95 9.76ms/24 flows, steps 0.6ms, changes 16.74ms, similar 1.79ms/95 candidates, Mac PGlite, environment-relative), CI test green locally, web/node/worker suite green, python untouched and green, graft green? Any production-SLO claim from PGlite numbers?

reliability.instructions: Any nondeterminism or resource risk: no wall-time assertions anywhere (numbers are recorded, never gated), fixed seed sizes, bounded corpus caps via CLI args with positive-int fallback, PGlite fixture per run with close in finally, subprocess timeout 120s?

scope.instructions: Anything beyond the perf baseline: transplant, product changes, new tools/routes, embeddings, billing, UI, alert/monitoring implementation, or unrelated refactors? Are SLOs/alerts correctly left to the P15 follow-on rather than claimed here?

security.instructions: Does the grain weaken any control: synthetic fixture only, no secrets, no network, actor-scoped reads (owner actor), no shell beyond the CI test's own node spawn of the repo script?

state.change: AC-00 perf baseline: scripts/bench_board_changes.mjs (4 ops, fixed corpus, p50/p95/max JSON) plus tests/node/bench-board-changes.test.mjs (exit-zero plus schema proof). No gates, no product change.
